data.title: Java Foundations
data.description: Build a foundation in objects, collections and dependable Java code.

lessons.title: Objects and responsibility
lessons.body: A class defines state and behavior; an object is an instance of that class. Keep each class focused on one responsibility. Encapsulation protects state behind methods rather than exposing mutable fields. Use an interface when callers should depend on a contract instead of one implementation.
lessons.exercise: Design a Candidate class with private name and email fields. Add a method that validates an email before updating it.

lessons.title: Choose the right collection
lessons.body: A List preserves order and allows duplicates. A Set models unique elements. A Map associates keys with values. ArrayList provides constant-time indexed access; insertion in the middle shifts elements. HashMap uses hashCode and equals to find keys. Mutable keys can break lookup when their hash changes.
lessons.exercise: Store unique candidate emails in a HashSet, then group candidates by skill using a Map<String,List<Candidate>>.

lessons.title: Handle failures clearly
lessons.body: Checked exceptions must be caught or declared. Unchecked exceptions usually represent programming errors or invalid state. Catch exceptions where you can recover or add useful context. Use try-with-resources for AutoCloseable resources. Do not hide a failure with an empty catch block.
lessons.exercise: Write a file-reading method with try-with-resources. Explain how you would report a missing resume file to the user.

data.title: React Essentials
data.description: Create interactive interfaces with components, state and effects.

lessons.title: Build reusable components
lessons.body: A React component describes UI from props and state. Props flow from parent to child and should be treated as immutable. Use stable keys when rendering lists so React can preserve the identity of each row. Split reusable presentation from application state where it improves clarity.
lessons.exercise: Create a CourseCard component that receives title, difficulty and an onOpen callback.

lessons.title: Manage state updates
lessons.body: useState stores values between renders. Use functional updates when the next value depends on the previous one. Never mutate arrays or objects held in state; create a new value. Derive values such as completed lesson count from source data instead of keeping a second copy that can drift.
lessons.exercise: Implement a bookmark toggle using setItems(previous => ...), without mutating the previous array.

lessons.title: Fetch data and clean up
lessons.body: useEffect synchronizes a component with external systems. List relevant dependencies. Clean up subscriptions, timers and object URLs. A stale network response can overwrite newer state, so use an AbortController or ignore results after cleanup. Render loading and failure states explicitly.
lessons.exercise: Fetch a course list on mount, show loading and error messages, and prevent an unmounted component from applying results.

data.title: SQL and PostgreSQL
data.description: Query relational data and understand ownership and row access.

lessons.title: Filter and aggregate
lessons.body: WHERE filters rows before grouping. GROUP BY forms groups; HAVING filters aggregated groups. Use COUNT, SUM and AVG to summarize records. ORDER BY controls result order. SQL NULL means missing or unknown; compare it with IS NULL instead of equals.
lessons.exercise: Write a query to find candidates with at least three completed interviews, ordered by interview count.

lessons.title: Join related tables
lessons.body: An INNER JOIN returns matching rows. A LEFT JOIN retains all left rows even when no right row matches. Keep conditions that preserve left rows in the join condition when appropriate. Unique constraints and foreign keys protect relationships and prevent duplicate associations.
lessons.exercise: Join candidate profiles with interview records and include candidates who have not recorded an interview.

lessons.title: Protect data with RLS
lessons.body: Row Level Security evaluates access rules for each database row. A policy should check trusted identity, such as auth.uid(), rather than a user-submitted owner. An application authorization check and an RLS policy provide different layers of protection. Test both allowed and denied access.
lessons.exercise: Describe a policy where a candidate reads their own records and a recruiter reads them only after an explicit consent grant.

data.title: API Test Automation
data.description: Practice request validation, authorization and reliable API checks.

lessons.title: Test the HTTP contract
lessons.body: An API contract includes route, method, authentication, input shape, status and response fields. A successful status alone is insufficient: check the expected body and persistent side effects. Validate missing fields, malformed JSON and boundaries as well as happy paths.
lessons.exercise: List checks for a POST resume endpoint: missing text, valid text, invalid token and forged owner.

lessons.title: Verify role boundaries
lessons.body: Authorization tests prove who can perform an action, not just who can log in. Test a candidate attempting an admin action, an unlisted recruiter, and a recruiter without candidate consent. Also verify revocation blocks future reads. Keep test accounts and data isolated.
lessons.exercise: Write a test matrix for candidate, recruiter and administrator access to a private recording.

lessons.title: Use fixtures and meaningful assertions
lessons.body: Fixtures create repeatable setup and cleanup. Mock an external provider to test local behavior, then run separate integration checks against the configured provider. A mocked test does not prove remote RLS or OAuth configuration works. Assert outcomes instead of copying implementation details.
lessons.exercise: Design one test that uploads a recording, grants access, verifies playback permission, revokes access and verifies denial.

data.title: Python Backend Basics
data.description: Build clear endpoints with validation and async service calls.

lessons.title: Validate at the boundary
lessons.body: Validate request structure and business rules before writing data. Type annotations document expectations; runtime validators enforce them. Normalize emails consistently. Return a useful error without leaking tokens or private upstream responses. Never trust a browser-provided role or score.
lessons.exercise: Create a Pydantic request model for a profile with a name, headline and limited skills list.

lessons.title: Understand asynchronous I O
lessons.body: async functions can yield control while awaiting network I O. Use an async HTTP client for concurrent service calls. Do not perform slow blocking work directly in an async request handler. Reuse clients with application lifespan and configure timeouts.
lessons.exercise: Explain why a shared HTTPX AsyncClient is useful for calls to Supabase.

lessons.title: Separate application concerns
lessons.body: Keep routing, data access and scoring logic separable. Routes enforce authentication and validate input; service helpers perform reusable work. Unit tests can cover pure scoring functions while endpoint tests cover authorization and persistence. Use environment configuration instead of hardcoded secrets.
lessons.exercise: Outline an endpoint that accepts answers, recalculates a test score and saves the verified result.

data.title: Interview Communication
data.description: Structure answers and explain project decisions with examples.

lessons.title: Use a structured answer
lessons.body: For behavioral questions, explain the Situation, Task, Action and Result. Keep the situation short and focus on what you did. Use only outcomes you can support. Technical answers benefit from stating assumptions, explaining an approach, and discussing tradeoffs.
lessons.exercise: Draft a STAR answer about a difficult deadline using an example from your own work.

lessons.title: Explain a project clearly
lessons.body: Start with the problem and users. Describe your contribution, architecture, important choices and testing. Explain one limitation honestly. Separate implemented features from proposed improvements; listing tools does not explain what they did.
lessons.exercise: Explain SmartHire's login, resume scoring and interview recording in two minutes.

lessons.title: Review recorded practice
lessons.body: Watch a practice recording and compare the transcript with what was said. Look for clear examples, concise explanations and unanswered parts of the question. Pace and filler counts are rough indicators, not confidence or correctness scores. Choose one specific improvement for the next session.
lessons.exercise: Record a mock interview and note one answer to shorten and one answer that needs a concrete example.
